issue.title: Record a decisions-web strand for the machine artifact-link write lane (hidden host-owned clones, never the primary)
issue.description:
Epic sase-y3 ("Keep machine artifact-link mutations out of primary sidecar clones")
established a durable architectural invariant that is currently recorded nowhere in
sase memory: only in the epic's plan file and its code comments. Phase sase-y3.4
proposed capturing it as a decisions-web record (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1); the
epic's land agent is filing it because phase workers may not create beads.

Per the decisions-web policy, phase workers and land agents must not write memory
files directly, so this task carries the proposed record for a worker with the
user's explicit permission to run the memory-write path.

task_type_fields.proposed_change:
Add a new decisions-web strand recording the invariant epic sase-y3 established.

Claim: SASE machine (background) artifact-link mutations never target the sidecar
clones nested under a project's primary (human) workspace checkout. The machine write
lane is the hidden host-owned clone at `~/.sase/projects/<key>/repos/<role>`
(`hidden_sidecar_clone_dir`), following the agents-sidecar precedent; the primary's
nested `repos/<role>` clones are human-owned and converge only through the existing
pull-based `sync_primary_sidecar_role` auto-sync.

Why this over the alternatives:

- Committing from the primary (the pre-epic behavior, reached by a defaulted `user`
  mutation origin) makes host background jobs indistinguishable from the human and
  strands worktree dirt when the ownership gate refuses an honest `machine` origin.
- Relaxing `authorize_store_mutation`'s primary-#0 refusal would weaken the
  fail-closed ownership contract for every caller, not just link maintenance.
- Writing to a numbered workspace clone ties durable host state to an evictable lease.

Cost: a second on-disk clone per document sidecar role per project, and machine writes
become visible in the primary only after auto-sync runs.

Reopen condition: if hidden host-owned clones stop being materializable on demand, or
if the ownership contract gains a first-class machine lane into primary-nested clones.

Implementing code: `src/sase/sdd/_artifact_link_machine_store.py`
(`resolve_machine_artifact_link_store`), `AccessKind.HOST_OWNED_SIDECAR` and
`_hidden_sidecar_machine_context` in `src/sase/workspace_provider/`, and the
`project.primary_sidecar_link_dirt` doctor check.

Link it to [[decisions/...]] neighbors as appropriate and reference the epic plan
`plan:202609/machine_link_mutations_off_primary.md`.
